hypotheses.statement: The incident was caused by an expired TLS certificate on payments-gateway.internal, which caused the checkout-api payments-connector to fail TLS handshakes, leading to 502 errors on POST /v2/checkout/submit.

observed_facts.statement: Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired at 09:12:03Z. Observed 5xx ratio 0.184 for POST /v2/checkout/submit over a 5 minute window against an objective of 0.005.
Alert checkout-api-latency fired at 09:14:41Z. p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit rose from 240ms to 10400ms.
Release 2026.5.14-a was deployed to production at 09:09:52Z. Changes included copy edits to three checkout confirmation email templates and a dependency bump of the CSV export library.
Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed at 10:04:18Z. The 5xx ratio had already returned to 0.004 at 09:58:10Z.
checkout-api payments-connector began experiencing repeated outbound TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443 at 09:11:47Z. Error: certificate verify failed: certificate has expired.
checkout-api: POST /v2/checkout/submit was returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted 3 retries, correlated with payments-connector TLS failures.
checkout-api payments-connector outbound TLS handshakes to payments-gateway.internal:8443 succeeded again. Error rate returned to baseline at 09:57:55Z.
Trace 5f21c0: POST /v2/checkout/submit total 10402ms. Span payments.authorize 10388ms error, terminated by client timeout, no upstream response recorded.
Responder C from the payments-gateway team reported that the leaf certificate for payments-gateway.internal expired at 09:11:40Z, was rotated, and took effect at 09:57:50Z.
INC-7742 opened at 09:15:00Z, severity 1, title 'Checkout submit failing for all customers'. No customer-impact estimate was recorded.
INC-7742 marked resolved. Resolution note reads only 'rolled back and recovered' and does not mention the certificate rotation.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or configuration records identifying the owner and automation for the payments-gateway.internal certificate renewal.
open_questions.question: Who owns the renewal automation for the payments-gateway.internal host certificate, and why did it fail to renew before expiration?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Quantitative impact analysis or customer reports detailing the scope and severity of the outage.
open_questions.question: What was the actual customer impact (e.g., number of failed transactions, revenue impact, affected users) during the incident?

summary: The checkout-5xx incident was caused by an expired TLS certificate on the payments-gateway.internal service, leading to TLS handshake failures in the checkout-api payments-connector. This resulted in 502 errors and high latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit requests. The system recovered automatically after the certificate was rotated, coinciding with a rollback that was not the root cause. The incident ticket lacks details on root cause and customer impact.

timeline.statement: checkout-api payments-connector began experiencing TLS handshake failures due to expired certificate.
Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired due to high 5xx ratio for POST /v2/checkout/submit.
Alert checkout-api-latency fired due to high p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit.
Certificate rotation for payments-gateway.internal took effect.
payments-connector TLS handshake failures returned to baseline.
Alert checkout-api-error-ratio stopped firing as 5xx ratio returned to 0.004.
INC-7742 marked resolved with note 'rolled back and recovered'.
